title: The Tolerance Limit
description: Brasston's arbiter is a caliper. It holds the party against a specification and reports the deviation, and it has no clause at all for exceeding the spec — the only judgement it can return is how far off you are, in which direction.

steps.text: It was waiting on the run past the inn with its arms already open to the width of a man, and it closed them as each of the party came level with it, without hurry, the way a man checks a pipe he has checked ten thousand times. There was a scale engraved along the inside of each arm. The numbers ran out well before the end of the metal.

lines.speaker: The Tolerance Limit
lines.text: MEASURING. Hold still. Movement is recorded as deviation.

lines.speaker: The Tolerance Limit
lines.text: The specification. All parts are measured against the specification.

lines.speaker: The Tolerance Limit
lines.text: Everything that enters the district is a part. Some parts object. Objection is recorded as deviation.

lines.speaker: Bard
lines.text: What happens if something comes out BETTER than your specification?

lines.speaker: The Tolerance Limit
lines.text: No procedure is held for that condition. It has not arisen.

lines.speaker: Rogue
lines.text: So you'd scrap something good for being the wrong kind of wrong.

lines.speaker: The Tolerance Limit
lines.text: Out of tolerance is out of tolerance. The caliper does not take sides — that is the whole of its virtue.

lines.speaker: Cleric
lines.text: It's going to measure us whether we agree or not, isn't it.
